subject: Urgent: Crestpoint throughput & error spike after v3.1 quant deploy — exec attention requested
messages:
From: Claire Hammond <claire@crestpoint.capital>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Liu <tom.liu@crestpoint.capital>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Crestpoint: sudden throughput collapse & 500s after v3.1

Jonas —

We're seeing a hard regression in our production traffic since Redwood pushed v3.1 with the new quantization profile on 2027-05-01 23:00 UTC. Impact summary:

- P95 latency jumped from ~210ms to ~1.6s for our standard 512-token requests.
- Error rate (5xx) rose from 0.1% to 4.3% across hot routes.
- Peak throughput dropped ~40% despite identical request patterns.

We already rolled out client-side retries and throttling; that just hides the problem and causes tails to skyrocket. This is material for our SLAs and we have a board-level review scheduled Tuesday. We need an immediate mitigation plan and a rollback option.

Attached: logs (truncated), sample traces, and request IDs. Can your ops team revert to v3.0 or enable an emergency fallback? We need an ETA.

—Claire
Claire Hammond

Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 02:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Technical notes: v3.1 quant profile causing KV cache pressure and batch inefficiency

Quick technical summary (lots of detail below):

Findings so far:
- The v3.1 quant profile changes packing layout for key/value cache blocks which increases per-request KV memory by ~22% for the most common sequence lengths.
- Increased memory per-request reduces effective batch sizes on the host GPUs, causing throughput loss under the same concurrency limits.
- In certain cases, denser packing led to kernel choice selection that is optimized for latency on longer sequences but performs poorly for short hot-path requests (our customers' 64–512 token median).
- We are also seeing elevated mem-allocation contention on 2 of Crestpoint's dedicated nodes which correlates with 5xx spikes.

Attached: crestpoint_logs_20270502.zip (excerpts below). Request IDs mapped to trace spans show high mem alloc and fallback kernel timeouts.

Excerpt (log):
"[2027-05-01T23:03:12Z] req=rp-4f3a trace=span-zz mem_alloc=812MB (expected 670MB) kernel=kv_pack_v31 fallback=yes
[2027-05-01T23:03:12Z] req=rp-4f3a error=503 reason=kernel_timeout"

Immediate mitigations available:
- Emergency canary rollback to v3.0 profile (fastest, low risk).
- Hot-route override: pin specific routes to v3.0 while leaving v3.1 for other traffic (requires config push and small routing rule change).
- Runtime tune: force alternate kernel selection on affected GPU families (medium risk, needs test).

Risk/notes:
- Rollback is straightforward but we lose any quality improvements from v3.1.
- Route pinning is the least disruptive for Crestpoint and gives us time to reprofile the quant packer.

I will remain on the bridge and can run the rollback steps when we have approval.

Irene Choi
SWE, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: leadership@redwood.ai; marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Hammond <claire@crestpoint.capital>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 07:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec: Crestpoint urgent — v3.1 quant profile regression and recommended rollback

Team — quick executive summary for visibility / approval:

What happened:
- On 2027-05-01 23:00 UTC we deployed model v3.1 with an updated quantization packing profile. Within hours Crestpoint reported a 40% throughput drop, p95 latency increase to ~1.6s, and 4% 5xx rate on hot routes.

Customer impact:
- Crestpoint handles market-sensitive workloads; this is blocking customer SLAs and they have an internal exec review Tuesday. Potential revenue and retention risk if not addressed promptly.

Root cause (prelim):
- v3.1 quant packer increases per-request KV memory and triggers a suboptimal kernel path for short-sequence traffic; leads to reduced batching efficiency and mem contention. Irene's team has logs attached.

Recommendation (preferred):
1) Approve immediate emergency canary rollback to v3.0 for Crestpoint (10% -> 100% progression over 90m). This is low-risk and reversible.
2) Offer a good-faith credit for the SLA exposure (Marissa to propose amount).
3) Post-mortem + code fix: rework packer heuristics and add targeted perf tests for short-sequence hot paths.

If leadership approves, Irene's team will run rollback and I will coordinate customer comms. We will also open a JIRA (INF-7892) to track technical remediation.

Please reply ALL with approval or objections. Time is sensitive.

Jonas Weber
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
